title: ‘CM Vijay’ WhatsApp call promises Rs 11 lakh aid, Bengaluru man loses Rs 1 lakh

reading.body:
This is an impersonation fraud carried out through a synthetic video call. The failure sits at the point of contact between a member of the public and a face and voice presented as a public official, on a consumer messaging app that offers no verification of who is on the other end. The deepfake did not fail at a technical task. It succeeded at the task it was built for, which was to be believed by one person for the length of a call.

Nothing in the reporting establishes that any platform detected the call, flagged the account, or was asked to. The victim's own scepticism was the only check in the chain, and it came after the payments rather than before them. Catching this kind of operation would require verification of identity at the channel level, or a means for a targeted individual to confirm a claimed official's identity before money moves. Neither is described as existing here.

The case was registered under the Information Technology Act, and police urged the public not to trust such calls. It is not established who made the deepfake, whether the same operation targeted others, or whether any arrest followed. A registered case is not a finding of guilt against any identified person.

reports.title: ‘CM Vijay’ WhatsApp call promises Rs 11 lakh aid, Bengaluru man loses Rs 1 lakh

summary:
A 29-year-old security guard in Bengaluru named Ratikanta Giri received a WhatsApp video call on September 9 from someone using an AI-generated deepfake to pose as Tamil Nadu Chief Minister Vijay. The caller offered him Rs 11 lakh in financial aid and said a manager would arrange the transfer. The fraudster then demanded payments for exchange charges, a locked PIN, and a fake CBI fine. Giri paid over Rs 1.04 lakh through a digital payment app before refusing a further demand of Rs 50,000.

Giri contacted the cybercrime helpline 1930 and then approached Byappanahalli police, who registered a case under the Information Technology Act. This is the first deepfake case of its kind reported in the city. Police have urged people not to believe such calls or make payments based on similar claims.
